Dear Dr. Henderson,

Thank you for evaluating this 19-year-old female who recently established care at our clinic. She is an undergraduate student who takes no chronic medications, and her family medical background is non-contributory.

On physical exam, her stature is right at the 50th percentile, showing neither unusually short nor tall standing height. Her cranium is noticeably elongated in the anteroposterior axis, and she exhibits bilateral cheekbone flattening. Her ocular globes sit normally rather than deeply set. A recent slit-lamp exam and dilated ophthalmic screening revealed axial nearsightedness, but her ocular lenses are centered without subluxation or margin notches, and the retinae are fully flat and intact. Intraorally, she has a markedly vaulted roof of the mouth with prominent tooth crowding.

Musculoskeletal evaluation is notable for slender, disproportionately elongated digits and diffuse ligamentous laxity throughout her peripheral joints. However, she retains complete extension at both elbows. Her spine demonstrates a mild lateral curve, while the anterior thorax exhibits no sternal depression or protuberance. Her feet maintain normal plantar arching without fallen arches, and she has no groin herniations. Dermatologic assessment reveals supple skin without abnormal cutaneous tightness or visible stretch marks.

A baseline transthoracic echocardiogram was obtained due to a systolic click; this demonstrated systolic billowing of the mitral leaflets accompanied by an associated regurgitant jet. Importantly, her ascending aortic root dimensions were within normal limits, with no sign of aneurysmal dilation or intimal tearing.

I would be very grateful for your comprehensive clinical assessment and management recommendations.

Sincerely,
Dr. Evelyn Vance
